newsitem.title: CANADA: TimberWest buyout offers due next month.
newsitem.headline: TimberWest buyout offers due next month.

text.p: Final binding offers to buy TimberWest Forest Ltd are expected by mid-December, the company and its 52-percent owner Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd said Wednesday.
The lumber producer put itself up for sale in October and said Wednesday it has received "multiple non-binding expressions of interest."
The companies said they would proceed to the next stage in the sale process in which "a number of qualified potential purchasers" will conduct detailed due diligence and tour TimberWest's operations.

A Fletcher official declined to specify the number of potential buyers who would participate in this process. Last month the companies said they had received more than 20 initial expressions of interest.
TimberWest was wholly owned by Fletcher Canada until it was spun off in 1993. Fletcher Canada is in turn majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd.
The sale effort was prompted by Fletcher's decision to narrow its focus further on its paper business and a view that TimberWest stock was undervalued.

TimberWest has five sawmills in British Columbia with annual capacity of 685 million board feet of lumber and 1.5 million cubic meters of wood chips. It also has timber tenures with annual harvest of 4.2 million cubic meters of wood.
Spokesmen for the independent committee of directors overseeing the sale were not available for comment. At a share price of C$20.60, TimberWest has a market capitalization of about C$630 million.
